payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is a recognizable frog visible in the toilet bowl opening or directly at its rim?
node.criteria: Pass if a recognizable frog is visible within the bowl opening or directly at its rim. Fail if that region is assessable and contains no recognizable frog. Unknown if frog identity or visibility of that region is insufficient. Identify the candidate and its visible location; this check does not establish that the frog is inside the bowl or that the request is complete.
node.binding: Inspect the edited image using the source toilet as the reference. Distinguish the bowl opening and rim from the raised lid, tank, surrounding fixtures, and floor. Frogs exclusively on those other surfaces do not pass this check.

The reference label constrains the aggregate, but does not identify which visual fact is missing, so inspect the image and criterion for the specific ambiguity rather than forcing a partial result. Preserve unknown when evidence is genuinely unresolved, and keep transport/schema failures separate from visual judgments; the traces show valid, queried observations and no dependency failures.
s3: Repair the malformed binding (remove the truncated “(...)” and state the actual visual proposition) and keep this node focused on bowl-interior placement. The edited image shows a frog seated in the bowl cavity, so the traces’ pass is supported; do not reverse it merely to match the aggregate “partial.” The source has no frog, and the edit adds one in the bowl, while extra frogs on the lid and floor are unrelated. The mismatch may therefore lie in how the full program maps this support check to completion, not in this node’s visual finding. Make the binding explicitly use ancestor observations as context, not independent corroboration, and require an independent inspection of the edited image’s bowl boundary and candidate body position. Preserve pass when interior placement is clear, fail only when assessable evidence shows no candidate inside, and unknown for genuine occlusion/compositing ambiguity. Keep visual uncertainty distinct from transport/schema or dependency failures; none are reported here.
s2: Remove the truncated fragment and make the binding unambiguously assess only whether source-to-edit comparison shows a newly added frog whose body is visibly within the bowl cavity, distinguishing the cavity from the raised lid, tank, and floor. The edited image does show a frog in the cavity, so the repeated pass is supported for this progress check; do not flip it to match the aggregate partial label. Keep this node’s progress finding separate from the full-program completion decision, and use s1 only as candidate context—not as independent corroboration. Require direct inspection of the bowl boundary and candidate position; preserve unknown for genuine spatial ambiguity, and keep visual uncertainty distinct from transport, schema, or dependency failures (none are reported).
